heard: The longest phantom planet hunt in history lasted over 50 years. In 1859, mathematician Urban Laverrier noticed mercury straying from its Newtonian path by 43 arcseconds per century. Having already predicted Neptune through gravitational math, he deduced an unseen world inside Mercury's orbit was tugging it. Soon, an amateur observer reported its transit across the Sun, earning the Legion of Honor for discovering Vulcan. Expeditions chased total solar eclipses, and professional astronomers even reported spotting the blazing world. Then, in 1915, Albert Einstein plugged Mercury into his brand-new theory of general relativity. The sun's mass was warping space-time itself, giving Einstein heart palpitations when his math matched Mercury without any extra planet. Space was bending, proving mankind had spent half a century chasing a ghost.
